label: Moral and epistemic parity: distinguish categorical force from irreducible favoring
summary: Read the primary-author arguments of Richard Rowland (2013, JESP), Jonas Olson (2018, Stockholm University accepted chapter) and Alex Murphy (2020, UCL open-access paper). Rowland defends a categorical-epistemic-reason route from a strong moral error theory denying all categorical reasons. Olson supplies a concrete functional alternative: reasons for belief are performance-to-belief-function standards, not irreducibly normative favoring, so moral-reason denial can coexist with some epistemic reasons. Murphy challenges this disparity by applying the error theorist's own rhetorical-authority argument to epistemic discourse and by testing whether moral judgments can also be understood functionally. Existing F6 is only a thin reason existential, and the stronger preference-independent epistemic authority still differs from irreducibility; neither can be silently identified with an irreducibly categorical reason. The current two-kind adoption model shows moral reason denial and epistemic adoption reasons coexisting, but has no functional/irreducibility distinction. Two research forks now identified: global irreducible-reason denial plus irreducible epistemic witness is inconsistent; moral-only error theory remains compatible with an epistemic witness unless a distinct positive moral reason or relevant cross-domain transfer is supplied. The belief-inquiry-action feedback loop illustrates practical interaction but does not by itself add a moral norm. No new attributed claim, theorem, worldview defeat or root premise closure. Detailed comparison in docs/notes/self-undermining-views.md. Continuation reconciled draft #1502 with main 80dbecadc. Exact theorem inspection distinguishes instrumental aim-conditioned force from constitutive functional correctness: preference independence does not defeat the latter or establish irreducibility. A matched safety-report trial separates belief correction, inquiry/action, and directed reliance duties. Removing the recipient or undertaking while preserving evidence isolates the missing transfer; adding invited reliance supplies a defeasible positive moral rationale with its categorical warrant explicitly open. Strong functional moral-only and rights-enriched realist alternatives survive. Full proposed outcome and rejection reasons are in the existing linked note, awaiting parent semantic challenge. No new theorem or root connection. Follow-through compares invited reliance with innocent misunderstanding at fixed present knowledge, injury and correction cost: undertaking-only and general rescue principles differ in source and scope; identical correction verdicts do not identify directed responsibility. Neither principle is derived from epistemic answerability.
blocker: Strong epistemic force still needs actual-force and answerability warrant, and an additional irreducibility bridge if global irreducible denial is targeted. Moral transfer requires defending a scoped categorical reliance/protection principle; directed demand needs separate standing. The moral-to-governance-to-GOD_4 bridge to registered GodExists remains unbuilt. Next test: culpably invited reliance versus unavoidable reasonable misunderstanding, fixed injury/correction costs; do not repeat thin-F6 or genus-to-instance shortcuts. Follow-through completed that comparison conceptually; the live next dependency is the categorical easy-rescue principle for a nonresponsible observer, separate from any special undertaking or epistemic norm.
